rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 2 on two ropes, straight down the line of the route.
hazards: Inspect the slings on the bail trees before use.
rappel_detail.station: The top of pitch 4, at the double bail trees.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 2 on two ropes, to the base.
rappel_detail.anchor: the next station straight down the route
rappel_detail.station: The intermediate station partway down the route, reached by the first rappel.

wa_zool_patch.rappel_count_note: Two double-rope rappels straight down the route from the bail trees at the top of pitch 4. Lengths are not published, and no single-rope count is given, so carry two ropes.
wa_zool_patch.descent_text: From the anchors at the top of pitch 4 (double bail trees), make two consecutive double-rope rappels straight down the line of the route back to the base.

wa_kangaroo_temple_north_face.rappel_count_note: Three single-rope rappels on a 60 m rope is the common sequence; it can also be done as two double-rope rappels on 50 m ropes, which is a different set of stations rather than a different count of the same ones. No per-station distances are published, so none are listed: a 60 m rope doubled reaches 30 m, which bounds every rappel here, and a party reported a 50 m rope only just reaching the second station, so that one is nearer 25 m. accounts disagree on the top anchor — one describes three bolts with hangers and no chains, another describes chains — most likely a rebuild, so judge what is actually in place.

rappel_detail.notes: The one rappel, just over 100 ft back down into the Zipper: two ropes, or a 70 m rope folded double in a high-snow year.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed slings on a tree (not bolted)
hazards: A single 60 m rope folded double does not reach the base.
rappel_detail.station: From the dead-tree notch atop the couloir, downclimb a short, exposed stretch to the tree carrying fixed rappel slings.

wa_lane_peak_r1.rappels: 1 rappel of just over 100 ft from a slung tree below the dead-tree notch back into the couloir; two ropes, or a 70 m in a high-snow year
wa_lane_peak_r1.descent_text: Two descent options are used depending on conditions and whether the party continues to the true summit. Direct reversal (the usual bail line): from the dead-tree notch atop the couloir, downclimb a short stretch of exposed terrain to the tree, which carries fixed rappel slings (a natural, sling-on-tree anchor — not bolted), and make one rappel back down into the Zipper. The rappel is typically just over 100 ft (roughly 30+ m), so it requires a double-rope rappel — two ropes joined, or a single rope doubled — to reach the base cleanly; in a high-snow year a single 70 m rope may just reach, with some downclimbing to finish. From the bottom of the rappel, downclimb/plunge-step the remaining couloir and the debris apron back into the basin and reverse the approach to Tatoosh Creek and the road. Summit-and-walk-off option: instead of rappelling, many parties traverse climber's left from the top of the couloir until the summit slopes come into view and continue to Lane Peak's true summit (a running belay or short pitch on the last 200-300 ft is sometimes prudent), then descend via the standard South Face gully/saddle walk-off shared with the Classic Route (down to the 5,440 ft Lane-Denman saddle, through the timber, down the talus to Tatoosh Creek, and back to the road) — longer, but avoids the rappel entirely. Hazards: rockfall/spindrift funneling into the couloir from above, a real chance of a stuck rope on rock features during the rappel, and avalanche/wet-slide hazard in the basin and lower couloir on both the approach and the descent, particularly once the sun hits the face.

wa_tooth_and_claw.rappels: Most parties walk off: an exposed 4th-class traverse west from the East Shoulder into the East Face descent gully. Rappelling the route is the alternative, on two 70 m ropes from a bolted station 20-30 ft above the old pitch-6 slung block to the bolted anchor atop pitch 5, then down the route on bolt and tree anchors; no count of rappels is published.
wa_tooth_and_claw.rappel_count_note: No source publishes a rappel total for this route, and the count moves with where you start, so no per-station distances are listed. The rope requirement is published and it is not a preference: the top station is a bolted anchor roughly 20-30 ft above the old pitch-6 slung-block anchor, and from it two 70m ropes reach the bolted anchor atop pitch 5 while doubled 60m ropes do not. A 70m lead rope plus a 70m tagline is the stated ideal because it keeps the option of rappelling from the very top; a party on doubled 60s has to break the first rappel at a fixed nut-and-sling anchor about halfway down pitch 6. Most parties do not rappel this at all — they top out on the East Shoulder and take the walk-off, a very exposed and sketchy 4th-class traverse west into the descent gully, which most keep the rope on for despite poor protection.
wa_tooth_and_claw.descent_text: Two real options, and most parties take the walk-off. Option 1 (walk-off): from the East Shoulder, make an exposed, somewhat sketchy 4th-class traverse west (it borders on unprotected 5th-class slab in spots, so many parties stay roped) to gain the same descent gully used off the East Face. Downclimb the gully, then traverse north (right) to pick up the climbers'/cattle trail that runs up to Liberty Bell, which drops you onto the Blue Lake Trail; a faint climbers' path cuts off a final stretch of trail before the highway. Option 2 (rappel the route): from the top, the first anchor is a bolted station roughly 20-30 feet above the old P6 slung-block anchor. With double 70m ropes (a 70m lead line plus a 70m tag line) you can rappel from the very top of the route; doubled 60m ropes will not reach that first station. If you're bailing from above the P5 crux rather than finishing the route, two 60m ropes are workable using a fixed nut-and-sling anchor partway down P6 as an intermediate station — anything shorter risks coming up short between anchors. Lower down, the rappel stations are obvious, good-quality anchors on trees or bolts. Hardware is mixed vintage: some original 1989 5/16" bolts remain despite a post-2016 rebolting push, and at least one older fixed-nut/sling anchor is noted as aging — back up or inspect any anchor you didn't place yourself before weighting it.

rappel_detail.notes: First of four double-rope rappels down the East Face, starting near M&M Ledge.
rappel_detail.anchor: bolted anchor, climber's-left of M&M Ledge
hazards: The M&M Ledge anchor is two pieces of old fixed gear, a pin and a wire. A large and reportedly bomber horn sits up and left of it that would make a much better station and nobody has rigged it - carry cord if you want to use it
Because the line trends left rather than dropping straight down, a rope end blown or thrown off line is awkward to recover
rappel_detail.station: The rappels begin at M&M Ledge. From it, work climber's left to reach good bolts - the bolted stations are not directly beneath where the ledge drops you, and finding them is the only route-finding on this descent. If you rappel from the ledge's own anchor instead, that is a fixed piton and a fixed wire, and the rappel from it also trends climber's left.

rappel_detail.notes: Continues down the East Face line on double ropes.
hazards: Steep sustained face with nothing to stand on between stations - once on the rope you are committed to reaching the next anchor
rappel_detail.station: Second station on the bolted line down the East Face.

rappel_detail.notes: Continues down the East Face line on double ropes.
hazards: Anything knocked off a station here falls the full height of the wall
rappel_detail.station: Third station on the bolted line.

rappel_detail.notes: Final rappel, reaching the ground at the base of the East Face.
hazards: Talus and snow at the base of the face for much of the season
rappel_detail.station: Last rappel, essentially reaching the ground at the base of the East Face - the side you approached from, so this is where your pack is.

wa_a_servant_to_liberty.rappels: 4 double-rope rappels from bolted anchors down the East Face, on Thin Red Line’s rappel line from M&M Ledge; or scramble to the summit roped and take the standard Liberty Bell descent.
wa_a_servant_to_liberty.rappel_count_note: Rappelling this route means joining Thin Red Line’s descent at M&M Ledge. Four rappels off bolts, reached by working climber's left from M&M Ledge, and the description that gives that sequence assumes two ropes - four double-rope rappels essentially to the ground. Parties who first rappel from M&M Ledge's own fixed pin-and-wire anchor, which also trends climber's left, count five. No single-rope option is described for this line. The alternative descent, for parties who continue to the true summit rather than rappelling from the ledge, is the standard Liberty Bell notch route - a downclimb east to a two-bolt station and two rappels of about 25 m into the Liberty Bell-Concord notch - which is fewer rappels but lands on the opposite side of the mountain from the East Face approach and from your pack. Per-station distances are not published; the figures given assume near-full-length double-rope rappels.
wa_a_servant_to_liberty.descent_text: From the top, either scramble to the summit roped and take the standard Liberty Bell descent, or rappel with two ropes down Thin Red Line's line: rappel with two ropes off M&M Ledge (fixed pin/wire anchor), then move climber's-left to bolted anchors for four double-rope rappels back to the base — five rappels total, all on bolted stations after the first.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 4 on two ropes, down pitch 5 to the pitch-4 anchor.
rappel_detail.anchor: two bolts with fixed biners, top of pitch 5
rappel_detail.station: Top of the route, where it joins the top of pitch 7 of Thin Red Line.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 4 on two ropes, down pitch 4 to the pitch-3 anchor.
rappel_detail.anchor: two bolts with fixed biners, top of pitch 4

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 3 of 4 on two ropes. Skip the pitch-2 anchor and go straight to the pitch-1 anchor.
rappel_detail.anchor: two bolts with fixed biners, top of pitch 3
hazards: Do not stop at the pitch-2 anchor; the line is set up to go past it to pitch 1.
rappel_detail.station: The pitch-3 anchor. Parties who stop after pitch 3 start the descent here.

rappel_detail.anchor: two bolts with fixed biners, top of pitch 1

wa_liberty_and_injustice_for_all.rappels: 4 double-rope rappels down the route from the top of pitch 5, all from two-bolt anchors with fixed biners, skipping the pitch-2 anchor; 2 if you start from the top of pitch 3
wa_liberty_and_injustice_for_all.rappel_count_note: Rappel the route with two ropes, using each two-bolt anchor in turn except pitch 2, which you skip on the way from pitch 3 to pitch 1. That gives four from the top of pitch 5, and two for parties who stop after pitch 3. Pitch lengths are not published, so no rappel lengths are given; carry two ropes.
wa_liberty_and_injustice_for_all.descent_text: Rappel the route with two ropes; the descent is straightforward and every station is a two-bolt anchor with fixed biners. From the top of pitch 5, where the route joins the top of pitch 7 on Thin Red Line, rappel to the pitch-4 anchor and then to pitch 3. From the top of pitch 3, skip the pitch-2 anchor and rappel directly to the pitch-1 anchor, then to the ground: four rappels in all, or two for parties who stop after pitch 3. Alternatively, continue climbing on Thin Red Line from the top of pitch 5.
